title: Tier-aware geo fallback runbook and overflow suppression strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Context:
Redwood's Dedicated-first routing has previously defaulted to simple capacity checks and tier affinity for region selection, with hosted as a catch-all when dedicated is unavailable. We need a prescriptive operational playbook and a set of automated overflow-suppression controls that reduce incorrect failovers, limit cross-region cost spikes, and preserve latency SLOs for priority tenants.

Goal:
- Provide runbook procedures for operators during capacity stress or regional outages.
- Implement automated controls that suppress noisy overflow events (tenant-caused surges) and prefer cheaper/compatible model variants rather than wholesale switching to hosted.
- Ensure deterministic rollback and observability so PMs and SREs can tune policies per tenant.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Reduce unintended dedicated->hosted transactions by 45% on tier-P0 traffic during experimental window.
- Limit cross-region egress growth to <10% relative to baseline during overflow events.
- No increase in p95 latency >10% for P0 tenants after policy rollout.

Design summary (high level):
1) Tier-aware Region Scoring: compute per-request score combining tenant tier weight (P0/P1/P2), regional health (capacity_headroom normalized to GPU-seconds), and data-residency affinity. Requests prefer regions with highest score; scores are cached for 30s with event-driven invalidation.

2) Overflow suppression gates: before triggering cross-region fallback or hosted routing, evaluate a set of gates:
   - Short-term tenant burst detector (EWMA over 60s): if the tenant's request rate is > 5x baseline, apply probabilistic draining (sample 10-30%) rather than immediate failover.
   - Cost budget guard: if projected hourly egress or hosted cost delta exceeds tenant budget threshold, apply variant throttles instead of hosted.
   - Variant compatibility probe: if a quantized or smaller model variant exists that meets quality budget, prefer model variant fallback with rate-limited sampling to detect quality regressions.

3) Probabilistic variant sampling & circuit breaker: introduce a "variant probe" channel that routes 1% of traffic to candidate variant to monitor latency, token-usage, and quality (via lightweight eval hooks). If probe metrics are within threshold for 5m, increase to 10% and then 50% rollouts. A failure triggers immediate circuit-breaker back to primary.

4) Tenant-weight decay & preemption policy: define tenant weights that decay on sustained high-traffic intervals so a tenant that exhausts its burst allowance temporarily has reduced priority for cross-region migration for a cooldown window (configurable, default 15m).

Operational runbook (initial on-call steps):
- Detection:
  1. Alert: "region capacity stress" (threshold: region GPU headroom < 12% and sustained p95 latency > 1.25x baseline).
  2. Query routing scoreboard dashboard: panels -> region_scores, tenant_bursts, variant_probe_health.
- Triage:
  1. Identify top 5 tenants contributing to headroom consumption (dashboard link).
  2. For each P0 tenant, check tenant burst detector; if positive, trigger tenant scoped soft-throttle via admin API and notify SE/Customer.
- Mitigation options (in order):
  1. Increase region autoscale target (if within allowed scaling window).
  2. Enable candidate model variant probes for affected tenants.
  3. Apply tenant soft-throttle or tenant weight decay override for non-P0 tenants.
  4. As last resort, enable controlled cross-region routing with explicit allowed-region list and egress budget caps.
- Post-incident:
  1. Run quality sampling on variant routes vs baseline using saved prompts (eval set).
  2. Produce incident note listing root cause, which gates were crossed, and recommended tuning.

Monitoring & metrics to expose:
- region_score (float) per region per minute
- tenant_burst_ratio (float) 60s EWMA
- variant_probe_success_rate (pct) over 5m windows
- cross_region_egress_delta (bytes/hour) by tenant
- dedicated_to_hosted_count (count) by tenant and reason code

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): scoreboard service for region_score, tenant burst detector, and admin APIs for soft-throttle. Feature flags behind config:routing.runbook.v1
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): integrate variant_probe channel and circuit-breaker, add cost budget evaluation module, add telemetry hooks.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): rollout to 10% of customers; QPS-limited pilot, gather metrics and customer feedback.

Testing & rollout strategy:
- Unit + integration tests for scoring logic and gate predicates.
- Load test simulating tenant spikes with controlled traffic generator in staging.
- Canary rollout: first internal preview org -> 10% external tenants (segmented by tier) -> global.

Rollback criteria:
- p95 latency regression > 15% for P0 tenants during any 30m window after rollout.
- Dedicated-to-hosted increases > 10% for P0 tenants relative to pre-rollout baseline.

Open trade-offs and decisions needed:
- How aggressive should tenant-weight decay be (default 15m vs 5m)? Shorter reduces customer pain but increases risk of oscillation.
- Default cost budget for automatic suppression (should it be per-tenant or per-account?).
- Whether admin soft-throttle should be reversible by SRE only or also by SEs.

Next steps / action items:
- @Marcelo: prototype region_score cache and tenant burst detector in routing service (2w).
- @Aisha: draft operator runbook in Confluence and create dashboard templates (3d).
- Schedule safety review with Compliance if variant probe stores customer prompts temporarily (TBD).

References and artifacts:
- Dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/routing/region-scoreboard
- Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/REDACTED/tier-aware-fallback
- Load test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-loadtest/pull/142
- RFC: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfc/tier-region-fallback-v2
comments: 2026-02-18 - Marcelo Ruiz: Started a PoC for region_score; basic EWMA works. Found that 30s cache causes oscillation for regions with bursty traffic. Will switch to event-invalidation for node join/leave.

2026-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Added initial Confluence runbook draft and linked dashboard mockups. Need ops feedback on mitigation order; suggested adding explicit 'contact SE' step before tenant soft-throttle for enterprise customers.
2026-02-24 - Lina Cho (SRE): Reviewed mitigation steps. Agreed on tenant soft-throttle but requested an audit log entry whenever soft-throttle is applied. Marked as must-have for rollout.
2026-02-27 - Marcelo Ruiz: Implemented variant_probe channel skeleton (GH PR #2718). Probe telemetry is emitted via routing.metrics.variant_probe_* (staging).
2026-03-01 - Product Review (Rajiv Menon): Asked for a customer-visible explanation template to be created for support teams when a tenant is soft-throttled; assigned to PM.
2026-03-03 - Marcelo Ruiz: Integration tests added for circuit-breaker behavior; test simulates variant degradation and validates immediate fallback. Preparing canary config.
2026-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Updated ticket with rollout dates and added release tag runtime-1.22.\n
